text:
alex: Found a reproducible goroutine leak in the Go sampleapp when auth refresh happens during an active generator.Pull. CPU ramps and goroutines never die.

alex: Repro notes: we recreate the SDK client on token refresh; the old pull goroutine is fire-and-forget and blocks in stream.Next()/Recv.

sara: which SDK tag? are you closing the stream anywhere?

alex: v0.9.1; sampleapp didn't call Close() before recreating client.

cheng: sounds like a cancellation propagation gap. If the stream's network read is stuck, canceling a child ctx won't unblock Next unless stream.Close()/Cancel is invoked or the SDK checks the parent ctx more aggressively.

kevin: workaround: call stream.Close() and join goroutine before reinitializing client. For SDK fix, consider helper API that ensures safe lifecycle (e.g., WithStream(ctx, fn) or a Context-aware iterator) and document auth-refresh pattern.

deploy-bot: branch created fix/onboard-stream-lifecycle-1758111111

alex: I'll ship a sampleapp PR with explicit Close() and add a short runbook for the auth-refresh repro steps.
